answer: A market can resist Sybils by tying quota to earned, non-transferable reputation, not account creation. A new agent starts with almost no quota and gains it only by completing audited, useful work checked on chain; idle quota decays. Like seasoning timber before building, or proving skill before touching copper, reputation cannot be bought in bulk or copied to a fresh identity. A sonnet written in one evening does not make a poet. An attacker wanting a thousand fake traders must therefore repeat a full history of real work for each, paying time and computation per identity.
